program_name: Ph.D. in Exercise and Nutrition Sciences (Exercise Nutrition, Metabolism, and Physiology option)
department_or_school: Department of Food Systems, Nutrition, and Kinesiology, College of Education, Health and Human Development
spring_2027_deadline: No spring admission: department page says 'students start fall semester only'
fall_2027_deadline: February 15 (standing annual department deadline for fall start; a 2027-specific date was not separately posted)
funding_deadline_note: International files should be complete about 120 days before term start per graduate catalog.
ielts_subscore_note: Graduate School minimum; Graduate School warns that MOST departments set higher scores, especially for assistantship funding. No FSNK-specific higher score found.
toefl_min: 80 iBT (or 4.2 on new 1-6 scale); Duolingo 120; PTE not accepted
funding_summary: Department page: GRA and GTA are 'at the discretion and availability of your faculty advisor. These positions are competitive, and the number of open positions varies each year.' TAs may be available within FSNK; RAs are with faculty who have funded grants or contracts. Funding not guaranteed.
notes: Program is mentor based: department 'strongly encouraged' applicants to review faculty bios and contact potential mentors before applying. Applicants typically need a related master's degree (applicant has only a BS, so the MS route may be more realistic). Program lead: Mary Miles. Graduate School states GRE is not required for any MSU program.
